```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

if (file.exists("data/processed/hh_all.rds")) {
  hh_all <- readRDS("data/processed/hh_all.rds")
} else {
  src <- list.files("scripts", pattern = "^read_hh\\.R$", ignore.case = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  source(src[1])
}
hh_all <- hh_all |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(.x <= -9998, NA_real_, .x)))

# one row per tower and year (only years with >= 90 % of half-hours present)
annual <- hh_all |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site_id = site, year) |>
  summarise(complete = mean(!is.na(TA_F) & !is.na(P_F)),
            TA_mean  = mean(TA_F, na.rm = TRUE),
            P_sum    = mean(P_F, na.rm = TRUE) * n(),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(complete >= 0.9)

find <- function(p) list.files("data/external", pattern = p, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)[1]
bio <- read_csv(find("worldclim_bio_my_sites\\.csv$"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(site_id, igbp, lat, lon, BIO1, BIO12)

anom <- annual |>
  left_join(bio, by = "site_id") |>
  mutate(dT = TA_mean - BIO1, dP = P_sum - BIO12, dP_pct = 100 * dP / BIO12)

soil <- read_csv(find("soilgrids_my_sites\\.csv$"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(property %in% c("clay", "sand", "soc"), bottom_cm <= 30) |>
  mutate(w = bottom_cm - top_cm) |>
  group_by(site_id, property) |>
  summarise(value = weighted.mean(mean, w), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = property, values_from = value)

site_static <- bio |> left_join(soil, by = "site_id")
```

## E1. Question and hypothesis

**Question:** Are the years measured at my five flux towers warmer and drier than the 1970–2000 climate normal at the same location?

**Hypothesis:** The mean annual temperature at every tower is above the WorldClim normal (BIO1), and the warming is largest at the northern towers (DE-Tha, US-MBP), because high latitudes have warmed fastest. For precipitation (BIO12) I expect no consistent direction, because changes in rainfall are regional and much less uniform than warming.

**Why my towers:** the question needs only air temperature and precipitation, so it works for all five towers, including CN-Dan, which has no carbon-flux data in my files. The towers span a wide range of climates (tropical, temperate, boreal peatland, alpine).

## E2. Data

| Dataset | Variables used | Spatial resolution | Time resolution and period | Downloaded on | Script and changes | Citation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLUXNET (v1.3_r1) | `TA_F`, `P_F` | tower footprint (~100 m–1 km) | half-hourly, 1996–2026 (varies by tower) | [date from Block 4] | Block 4 download script, unchanged | see E6 |
| WorldClim 2.1 | BIO1, BIO12, monthly `tavg` and `prec` | 5 arc-minutes (~9 km) | 1970–2000 normal | 26 Nov 2026 | `02_worldclim.R`, unchanged | Fick & Hijmans (2017), see E6 |
| SoilGrids 2.0 | clay, sand, soil organic carbon (0–30 cm, plus other properties in the data) | 250 m | static | 26 Nov 2026 | `04_soilgrids.R`, unchanged | Poggio et al. (2021), see E6 |

My two datasets at the five towers:

```{r}
#| label: site-table
site_static |>
  transmute(Tower = site_id, IGBP = igbp, `Lat (°)` = round(lat, 2), `Lon (°)` = round(lon, 2),
            `BIO1 (°C)` = round(BIO1, 1), `BIO12 (mm)` = BIO12,
            `Clay (%)` = round(clay, 1), `Sand (%)` = round(sand, 1), `SOC (g/kg)` = round(soc, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## E3. Methods

**Download:** I ran `02_worldclim.R` and `04_soilgrids.R` once each on 26 Nov 2026 without changing them. [Add anything that failed or any retry from your log.]

**Extraction:** the scripts took the value of each raster at the tower coordinates (WorldClim: the 5′ cell containing the tower; SoilGrids: the 250 m cell), in EPSG:4326.

**Processing:** −9999 was read as missing. For each tower and year I computed the mean air temperature (`TA_F`, °C) and the annual precipitation sum (`P_F`, mm, scaled to a full year from the mean of the available half-hours). Only years with at least 90 % of half-hours were used. The temperature anomaly is the yearly mean minus BIO1, and the precipitation anomaly is the yearly sum minus BIO12 (also shown in %). Soil properties are the 0–30 cm mean, weighted by layer thickness.

**Precipitation at US-MBP:** `P_F` at US-MBP equals the ERA5 precipitation (`P_ERA`) in every one of the 16 years, so it is not a tower measurement, and its yearly sums (1,913–3,224 mm) are about four times the WorldClim normal (692 mm). I could not find the cause and did not change any values. US-MBP is therefore excluded from the precipitation comparison but kept for temperature.

**Analysis:** the main result is the mean temperature anomaly over all tower-years, with n. I also show the anomalies per tower and year.

## E4. Results

```{r}
#| label: number
n_tab <- anom |> group_by(site_id) |>
  summarise(years = n(), mean_dT = round(mean(dT), 2),
            mean_dP_pct = ifelse(first(site_id) == "US-MBP", NA, round(mean(dP_pct), 1)))
n_tab |> knitr::kable(col.names = c("Tower", "Years (n)", "Mean temperature anomaly (°C)",
                                    "Mean precipitation anomaly (%)"))

anom |> summarise(towers = n_distinct(site_id), tower_years = n(),
                  mean_dT_all = round(mean(dT), 2)) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-temp
#| fig-cap: "Annual mean temperature anomaly per tower: tower mean minus WorldClim 1970–2000 BIO1. The dashed line is the normal."
ggplot(anom, aes(year, dT, colour = site_id)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() + geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Temperature anomaly (°C)", colour = "Tower") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-prec
#| fig-cap: "Annual precipitation anomaly (%) relative to the WorldClim BIO12 normal. US-MBP is excluded (see E3)."
anom |> filter(site_id != "US-MBP") |>
  ggplot(aes(year, dP_pct, colour = site_id)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() + geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Precipitation anomaly (%)", colour = "Tower") +
  theme_minimal()
```

[One or two sentences: the overall mean temperature anomaly with n, which towers are warmest, and what happens with precipitation.]

## E5. Discussion

1. **Hypothesis:** [Warmer at all five towers: yes. Strongest at the northern towers: only partly. DE-Tha is among the highest, but US-MBP is lower than CN-Dan and AU-Ctr. Precipitation: describe what the figure shows.]
2. **Scale:** WorldClim cells are about 9 km, much larger than a tower's footprint of 100 m–1 km, so the normal is a regional average. This matters most at CN-Dan, where elevation changes quickly within a cell. SoilGrids cells (250 m) are closer to the footprint, but still coarser than the tower's own surroundings.
3. **Limitations:** [(a) the normals are interpolations from weather stations, while my yearly values come from tower sensors, so part of the difference may be method and not climate; (b) some towers have few usable years (CR-Fsc has 4); (c) US-MBP precipitation could not be used. With more time I would compare against a second reanalysis.]
